column1: charisma§His charisma filled rooms that his arguments could not, and the party won three elections on it before the arguments mattered.§他的**个人魅力**填满了他的论点填不满的房间，靠着它政党赢了三次大选，之后论点才变得要紧。§
charitable§The most charitable reading of the memo is that its author had not read the report he was summarizing.§对这份备忘录最**宽厚的**理解是：作者没读过他正在概述的那份报告。§car（亲爱，同 cherish 珍爱）
charlatan§The charlatan sold nine thousand bottles before a chemist bothered to test one and found it was sugar water.§这个**江湖骗子**卖出九千瓶，才有一位化学家肯化验一瓶，结果发现是糖水。§
cheapen§Endless discounts cheapened a brand that had spent forty years persuading people it was worth the price.§没完没了的打折**贬低**了一个花四十年说服人们它值这个价的品牌。§
cheerfully§She cheerfully rewrote the chapter a fourth time, which unnerved the editor far more than complaining would have.§她**高高兴兴地**第四次重写这一章，这比抱怨更让编辑不安。§
cherish§He cherishes a photograph of a day he cannot remember, taken by someone whose name nobody in the family knows.§他**珍爱**一张自己记不得那天的照片，拍摄者的名字家里没人知道。§
chicanery§The chicanery was buried in an appendix: a definition of "revenue" that no accountant outside the firm would recognize.§这套**诡辩伎俩**藏在附录里——一个公司之外没有会计认得的「营收」定义。§
chide§His mother chided him gently for the interruption, and he apologized to a room that had not noticed it.§母亲为他的插话温和地**责备**了他，他便向一屋子根本没察觉的人道了歉。§

chronicle§The chronicle records eleven floods, four famines, and the exact day the bell tower fell, but never once names the writer.§这部**编年史**记下十一次洪水、四次饥荒和钟楼倒塌的确切日期，却从未提及作者的名字。§chron（时间，同 chronology 年表）
churlish§It would be churlish to complain about the seats when the whole concert was free and the playing was superb.§整场音乐会免费、演奏又极出色，为座位抱怨未免**小气无礼**。§
circuitous§The explanation was so circuitous that by the end nobody could say whether he had answered the question or not.§这番解释**兜圈子**兜到最后，没人说得清他到底有没有回答那个问题。§circu（绕圈，同 circle 圆）+ it（走，同 exit 出去）
circumlocution§Three paragraphs of circumlocution stood in for one sentence the writer clearly did not want to put on record.§三段**绕来绕去的话**代替了一句作者显然不愿留下记录的话。§circum（周围）+ loqu（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）

circumscribe§The charter circumscribes the mayor's power narrowly, which is why every big project here needs the council's signature.§市宪章严格**限定**了市长的权力，所以这里的每个大项目都需要议会签字。§circum（周围）+ scrib（写，同 describe 描述）→ 画一圈框住
circumspect§Auditors are trained to be circumspect, and hers is the rare report that says plainly what the numbers mean.§审计员受训要**谨慎**，而她那份报告罕见地直白说出数字的含义。§circum（周围）+ spect（看，同 inspect 检查）→ 四下张望
circumspection§A little more circumspection would have saved the campaign: one unverified photograph undid nine months of work.§多一点**审慎**本可救下这场运动——一张未经核实的照片毁了九个月的工作。§

circumvent§The design circumvents the patent by doing the same thing in a different order, and the courts have not yet decided whether that counts.§这个设计通过换个顺序做同样的事来**规避**专利，法院尚未判定这算不算数。§circum（周围）+ vent（走，同 event 事件）→ 绕道走过去
clairvoyant§Her memo now looks clairvoyant, though at the time it was simply the only one that read the shipping data carefully.§她那份备忘录如今看着像**未卜先知**，可当时它不过是唯一认真读过船运数据的一份。§clair（清楚）+ voir（看见）
clandestine§The clandestine meetings continued for two years in a building owned, as it turned out, by the ministry watching them.§这些**秘密的**会面持续了两年，而会面所在的楼，结果正属于监视他们的那个部。§clandes（隐藏）
clarity§The clarity of the diagram did more for the proposal than forty pages of text had managed in three months.§这张图的**清晰**在三个月里为方案做的贡献，超过四十页文字所能做到的。§clar（清楚，同 clear 清楚的）
cleanse§Six weeks of rain cleansed the air over the valley, and for the first time in years the far ridge was visible.§六周的雨**净化**了河谷上空的空气，多年来头一回能看见远处的山脊。§
clientele§The restaurant's clientele changed entirely when the factory closed, and the menu followed within a year.§工厂关闭后这家餐馆的**客户群**完全变了，菜单一年内也跟着变。§client（受保护者）
clinical§Her tone was clinical rather than cold: she described her own diagnosis the way she would describe a stranger's.§她的语气是**临床式**的而非冷漠——她描述自己的诊断就像描述陌生人的。§clin（卧床，同 recline 斜倚）→ 病床边的
cloy§The sweetness cloys after two bites, which is why the dish is served in portions the size of a walnut.§这种甜**吃两口就腻**，所以这道菜的分量只有核桃大小。§
clumsily§He clumsily raised the subject at dinner, and what should have taken five minutes consumed the entire evening.§他在晚饭时**笨拙地**提起这个话题，本该五分钟的事耗掉了整个晚上。§
clutter§Clutter, not shortage, was the problem: the warehouse held everything they needed and nobody could find any of it.§问题在于**杂乱**而非短缺——仓库里该有的都有，可谁也找不到。§
coalesce§The scattered protests coalesced into a single movement the week the government banned all four of them at once.§政府一周内同时禁掉四场抗议，零散的抗议就**汇合**成了一场运动。§co-（一起）+ alesc（长大，同 adolescent 青少年）
coalition§The coalition held for nineteen months, which is nine months longer than anyone who negotiated it had expected.§这个**联合政府**维持了十九个月，比任何谈成它的人预期的多了九个月。§
coddle§Coddling the prototype kept it running through the demonstration and taught them nothing about how it would fail in the field.§**呵护娇养**着样机让它撑过了演示，却没让他们学到它在现场会怎么失效。§
coerce§No one coerced her into signing; she simply understood that the alternative was losing the only work in town.§没人**强迫**她签字，她只是明白另一个选择是失去镇上唯一的工作。§co-（一起）+ erc（约束）
cogent§The most cogent objection came from a first-year student who asked what happened when the sample was ten times larger.§最**有说服力**的反驳来自一名一年级学生，他问样本大十倍时会怎样。§co-（一起）+ ag（驱动，同 act 行动）→ 把人推到同一结论
cognition§Sleep loss damages cognition long before people notice it, which is why the pilots kept scoring themselves as fine.§睡眠不足在人们察觉之前很久就损害**认知**，所以那些飞行员一直给自己打「状态良好」。§co-（一起）+ gn（知道，同 know 知道）
cognizant§The board was fully cognizant of the risk and approved the launch anyway, which is what the minutes now prove.§董事会完全**知晓**这一风险，却仍批准了发布，会议记录如今证明的正是这一点。§
coherent§For the first time the argument was coherent: each section now followed from the one before instead of standing alone.§论证第一次变得**连贯**——每一节都从前一节推出来，而不再各自为政。§co-（一起）+ her（黏，同 adhere 附着）
cohesive§What made the team cohesive was not friendship but a shared conviction that the deadline was genuinely impossible.§让这支团队**紧密团结**的不是友谊，而是一个共识：这个期限是真的做不到。§
collaborator§Her collaborator did the fieldwork for eleven years and appears on the title page in smaller type.§她的**合作者**做了十一年田野调查，署名却以更小的字号排在扉页上。§col-（一起）+ labor（劳动）
collage§The collage uses no paint at all: ticket stubs, receipts, and a bus map, arranged until they read as a face.§这幅**拼贴画**完全不用颜料——票根、收据和一张公交线路图，摆到能读成一张脸为止。§

colloquially§Colloquially the word means something close to "cheap," though every dictionary still gives only the older, technical sense.§这个词**口语中**的意思接近「廉价」，尽管所有词典仍只收录更旧的技术义。§col-（一起）+ loqu（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）
combat§The unit combated the fire for nine days with equipment designed for buildings, not for forty square miles of forest.§这支队伍用为建筑物设计的装备**扑救**了九天山火，而火场有四十平方英里森林。§com-（一起）+ bat（打，同 battle 战斗）
comical§The effect was comical rather than frightening: a two-meter dragon that squeaked whenever the operator moved its jaw.§效果**滑稽**而非可怕——两米长的龙，操作者一动它的下巴就吱吱作响。§
commandeer§Troops commandeered every truck in the district, and the harvest rotted in fields nobody could reach.§部队**征用**了全区所有卡车，收成烂在了谁也到不了的地里。§
commemorate§The plaque commemorates eleven men who died in a mine that the company insisted, for decades, had been safe.§这块牌匾**纪念**十一名死于矿难的工人，而公司数十年来一直坚称那座矿是安全的。§com-（共同）+ memor（记忆，同 memory 记忆）

commend§The judge commended the officer's restraint, noting that a drawn weapon would have ended the evening very differently.§法官**嘉许**了这位警员的克制，指出如果拔枪，那晚的结局会截然不同。§com-（加强）+ mend ← mand（托付，同 mandate 命令）
commendable§The effort was commendable and the result was not, and the report manages to say both without embarrassment.§努力**值得称道**，结果则不然，这份报告把两点都说了，还不显尴尬。§
commendation§The commendation came eleven years late, by which time two of the three recipients had already died.§这份**嘉奖**迟到了十一年，那时三位受奖者中已有两位去世。§

commiseration§His commiseration was genuine but useless: he had never lost a job and could not imagine what the week actually cost her.§他的**同情**是真的，却没用——他没失过业，想象不出那一周对她意味着什么。§com-（一起）+ miser（悲惨，同 miserable 悲惨的）
commodity§Water became a traded commodity here in 1994, and the price of an acre-foot has since risen more than tenfold.§水在这里于 1994 年成了可交易**商品**，此后每英亩英尺的价格涨了十倍不止。§commod（方便／合用，同 accommodate 容纳）
commonness§The commonness of the name defeated the search: four hundred people in the city shared it, and thirty shared the birthday too.§这个名字之**普通**让搜寻落了空——全市四百人同名，其中三十人连生日都相同。§
commonplace§Rooftop solar was exotic in 2005 and commonplace by 2020, and nothing about the physics changed in between.§屋顶光伏在 2005 年还稀奇，到 2020 年已**司空见惯**，其间物理原理毫无变化。§
community§The community rebuilt the bridge itself after two years of waiting, and the county later billed it for the permit.§等了两年后，这个**社区**自己重建了桥，郡里后来还就许可证向它收了费。§commun（共同，同 common 共同的）
comparability§The comparability of the two datasets is doubtful: one counts households and the other counts individuals.§两套数据的**可比性**很成问题——一套统计家庭，另一套统计个人。§
comparable§No comparable city has tried this, so the council is arguing from a single example on another continent.§没有**可比的**城市试过这个，所以议会只能拿另一个大洲的孤例来论证。§com-（一起）+ par（相等，同 par 平价）

compassionate§The compassionate response would also have been the cheap one, which makes the decision harder to explain, not easier.§**富于同情心的**做法同时也是便宜的做法，这让那个决定更难解释，而非更容易。§com-（一起）+ pass（受苦，同 passion 受难）→ 一同受苦
compatibility§Compatibility with the old files was the only reason anyone kept the software, and the new version quietly dropped it.§与旧文件的**兼容性**是人们还留着这软件的唯一理由，而新版悄悄取消了它。§
compatible§The two systems are compatible on paper and incompatible in practice, which cost the hospital eighteen months.§这两套系统在纸面上**兼容**，实际并不兼容，这让医院耗掉了十八个月。§com-（一起）+ pat（忍受，同 patient 病人）→ 能相处
compel§Nothing in the law compels disclosure, so the company published the figure only after a reporter had already found it.§法律并不**强制**披露，所以公司是在记者已经查到数字之后才公布的。§com-（一起）+ pel（推，同 propel 推进）
compendious§A compendious footnote covers two centuries of scholarship in nine lines and sends you to eleven books.§一条**简明扼要**的脚注用九行概括两个世纪的研究，并指向十一本书。§com-（一起）+ pend（称重，同 pendulum 摆）→ 称在一起、浓缩
competitive§The bidding was competitive only in form: three of the four firms were owned by the same holding company.§这场招标只在形式上**有竞争**——四家公司里有三家属于同一控股集团。§

complacent§Two profitable decades made the firm complacent, and it noticed the new competitor in the year it lost half its market.§二十年盈利让这家公司**自满**，等它注意到新对手时，已丢掉一半市场。§com-（加强）+ plac（取悦，同 please 使高兴）→ 自己让自己满意
complain§Residents complained about the noise for four years, and the file the council opened in 2019 contains every letter.§居民就噪音**投诉**了四年，市议会 2019 年建立的卷宗里存着每一封信。§

complement§The photographs complement the text rather than illustrate it: they show what the writer could not bring herself to describe.§这些照片**补足**而非图解文字——它们呈现了作者不忍描述的东西。§com-（一起）+ ple（填满，同 complete 完整的）
complexity§The complexity is administrative, not technical: eleven agencies must sign, and no two use the same form.§这种**复杂**是行政上的而非技术上的——十一个机构要签字，没有两家用同一张表。§
compliant§A compliant workforce is not the same as a willing one, and the difference showed up in the quality figures.§**顺从的**员工队伍不等于愿意干的队伍，差别体现在质量数据上。§

complicity§Her silence amounted to complicity, and she has said since that she understood this at the time and stayed quiet anyway.§她的沉默无异于**共谋**，她后来说自己当时就明白，却仍旧没出声。§com-（一起）+ plic（折叠，同 complicate 使复杂）→ 折在一起
complimentary§The complimentary review turned out to have been written by the author's former supervisor, a fact the journal never disclosed.§那篇**赞美的**书评原来出自作者从前的导师之手，期刊从未披露这一点。§
compound§Rising rents compound a shortage that was already severe, and each year's decision makes the next year's harder.§租金上涨**加剧**了本已严重的短缺，每一年的决定都让下一年更难。§com-（一起）+ pon（放，同 component 部件）
comprehend§Nobody in the room fully comprehended the contract, and eleven people signed it before the afternoon was over.§屋里没有人完全**理解**这份合同，而一个下午没过完就有十一个人签了字。§com-（完全）+ prehend（抓，同 apprehend 领会）→ 全抓住
comprehensible§The instructions became comprehensible only after a technician redrew them as six pictures with no words at all.§这些说明直到一位技师把它们重画成六张完全无字的图，才变得**可理解**。§
